objective.text: Distinguish an optional include from silently suppressing a template execution error.

difficulty.rationale: Separate an existence check from suppression of errors while rendering an existing view.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A layout uses @includeIf("banner"). The banner view exists but throws an application exception while rendering. Does includeIf make this an optional failure?

options.text: Yes; the view is rendered only if its variables have already passed validation.
options.rationale: View existence is the condition; input validation status is not consulted by includeIf.
options.misconception: View existence is the condition; input validation status is not consulted by includeIf.

options.text: Yes; every rendering exception becomes an empty string.
options.rationale: The directive does not promise to suppress runtime exceptions from an existing template.
options.misconception: The directive does not promise to suppress runtime exceptions from an existing template.

options.text: No view is rendered because includeIf always requires a separate boolean argument.
options.rationale: includeIf accepts the view name and optional data; a separate explicit condition is the role of includeWhen.
options.misconception: includeIf accepts the view name and optional data; a separate explicit condition is the role of includeWhen.

options.text: No; it skips a missing view, but errors inside an existing view still propagate.
options.rationale: includeIf checks whether the view exists before rendering it; it is not an exception-swallowing wrapper around that rendering.

explanation.summary: includeIf checks whether the view exists before rendering it; it is not an exception-swallowing wrapper around that rendering.
